question: A patient with persistent foreign body sensation and a linear vertical corneal abrasion should have the upper eyelid everted to look for a subtarsal foreign body.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. The diagnostic clue is vertical linear abrasions on the superior cornea — these are pathognomonic of a subtarsal FB on the inner upper eyelid. Always evert the upper lid in any patient with FB sensation, even if you cannot see a surface FB.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A subtarsal FB beneath the upper tarsal plate produces a characteristic pattern of multiple vertical linear corneal abrasions (scratch lines) as the rough FB wipes across the cornea with each blink. Upper lid eversion is mandatory — failure to evert the lid is the most common reason for a missed subtarsal FB.
